summary: The early life of Joseph Stalin in Gori and Tiflis, Georgia, from his 1878 birth through parental beatings, street fights, Russified schooling and seminary radicalisation to his 1899 expulsion as a young Marxist.

evidence.note: birth in Gori in 1878 opens the story
drunken father hurls the boy to the ground and hunts him at home
father beats the mother; she later beats the son harshly
Georgian banned in schools; harsh punishments, threat against teacher
Darwin leads him to atheism; enters the Tiflis seminary
publishes acclaimed poetry as a teenager under a pen name
organises a near-riot protest against a school inspector
turns to Marxism and forms a more militant study circle
expelled from the seminary in May 1899; story ends at adulthood

notes: Story only covers 1878-1899. covered_span runs to 1953 solely because of the lifetime rule for deep-dive person stories; this will surface the story under Soviet-era filters it barely touches. Roles reflect what he became plus his youthful protest and poetry. Primary theme picked for catalogue fit; child-abuse is the closest runner-up.
